question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $2x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,15)?$
question.worked_solution:
The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for $k\in Z,$ we have the following:

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)$

The modulus equals $15$ in all statements, which suggests we'll need to use the first property.

Notice that the coefficient of $x$ is $2,$ and $8\cdot 2=16$ is one larger than the modulus. Therefore, we can reduce the coefficient of $x$ to unity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ 8\cdot 2x & ≡8\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ 16x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+15x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+0x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Given that $w≡z\,(\text{mod}\,8),$ construct a statement that also must be true:

$$
{{field-1}}w≡{{field-2}}z\,(\text{mod}{{field-3}})
$$
question.worked_solution:
The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for $k\in Z,$ we have the following:

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)$

Let's multiply our congruence by $2$ and apply the second property.

$$
\begin{aligned}w≡z\,(\text{mod}\,8)\, & ⟹\,2\cdot w≡2\cdot z\,(\text{mod}\,2\cdot 8) \\ w≡z\,(\text{mod}\,8)\, & ⟹\,2w≡2z\,(\text{mod}\,16)\end{aligned}
$$

question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}94 & ≡11\cdot 8+6\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡11\cdot 0+6\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ 74 & ≡9\cdot 8+2\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡9\cdot 0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}94\cdot 74 & ≡6\cdot 2\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡12\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡8+4\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
94\cdot 74\text{ mod }8=4.
$$

question.problem: What is the last digit in the decimal expansion of ${28}^{18}?$
question.worked_solution:
If $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ and $c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),$ then the following properties hold:

- $ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- ${a}^{k}≡{b}^{k}\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ for any positive integer $k$

To find the last digit, we need to calculate the following residue:

$$
{28}^{18}\text{ mod }10
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & ≡20+8\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\cdot 10+8\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\cdot 0+8\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the exponentiation property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{28}^{2} & ≡{8}^{2}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡64\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 10+4\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ {28}^{6} & ≡{({28}^{2})}^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{4}^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡64\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 10+4 & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 0+4 & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we decompose ${28}^{18}$ into a product of smaller exponents. 

$$
{28}^{18}={({28}^{6})}^{3}
$$

By applying the multiplicative and exponentiation properties, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{28}^{18} & ≡{({28}^{6})}^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡(4)^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡64\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 10+4\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\cdot 0+4 & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{28}^{18}\text{ mod }10=4
$$

which means that the last digit of ${28}^{18}$ is $4.$
